title: Director - Corporate Continuous Improvement
text:
**Description**
****Position Summary****
The Director of Corporate Continuous Improvement (CI) leads MacAllister’s enterprise CI strategy, Corporate CI team, and improvement portfolio. In partnership with the owner, executive team, and divisional leaders, the Director helps establish and build alignment around MacAllister’s CI vision, strategy, priorities, and multi-year roadmap. The Director identifies and prioritizes high-value opportunities, builds organizational problem-solving capability, and leads improvement work from opportunity identification through execution and sustainment.
 
 
The role establishes CI standards, tools, and training; coaches, mentors, and influences leaders and teams across the organization; and communicates CI priorities, results, and opportunities for support.
 
 
The ultimate objective is to build and sustain a culture in which continuous improvement becomes habitual and is reflected in how leaders and employees think, act, solve problems, and improve the way work gets done.
 
 
****Position Duties/Responsibilities****
**Primary Responsibilities**

* Partner with the executive team, and divisional leaders to develop and maintain MacAllister’s CI strategy, multi-year roadmap, priorities, and operating model aligned with company goals. Build leadership alignment and shared ownership of CI priorities and expectations across the organization.
* Own CI project identification, prioritization, approval, execution, and close-out, focusing on where CI creates the most value; support employee-driven improvement alongside leader-sponsored initiatives.
* Maintain consistent project close-out documenting results, lessons learned, and sustainment plans; verify improvements and results are sustained and take corrective action as needed.
* Set organization-wide CI standards, tools, and terminology; guide Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, DMAIC, and PDCA application grounded in facts, data, and root cause analysis; coach project teams and facilitate select high-impact improvement events.
* Lead improvement-related change management, engaging affected employees early and ensuring process adoption and sustainment.
* Oversee CI training tailored to responsibility levels using consistent terminology and live projects; coach and support CI-trained departmental leaders who remain in their home departments outside CI.
* Define CI value primarily through capability measures—leaders solving problems independently, AI use cases adopted, and idea-to-approval cycle time—with financial results as supporting evidence.
* Communicate CI initiatives, results, and available support so leaders know when and how to engage the team; share success stories and recognize improvement contributors.
* Use coaching-first leadership to build team autonomy, confidence, and influence; foster problem reporting, experimentation, and learning from mistakes by supporting people publicly and coaching privately.
* Hire, develop, and manage CI personnel; oversee budget, resource allocation, and team structure as needs evolve.
* Play a leadership role in MacAllister’s Center of Practice for CI, AI, and problem-solving leadership, incorporating AI and other emerging technologies into CI methods where they improve problem solving, decision making, or productivity. Partner with MacAllister’s enterprise AI leadership on broader AI strategy, standards, and adoption.

**Supervisory Responsibilities**

* Directly supervises the Corporate CI team and oversees day-to-day operations of the CI department. Mentors and coaches CI team members to strengthen their capabilities as problem solvers, facilitators, coaches, and trusted business partners.
* Reviews and evaluates the work and performance of reporting employees; has authority for hiring and disciplinary actions.

****Position Requirements****
**Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in business, engineering, or a related field.
* 10 years or more of experience in continuous improvement, operations, or business transformation.
* 5 years or more of experience leading leaders.
* Proven success coaching others to identify and solve problems independently.
* Working knowledge of Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, DMAIC, and PDCA.
* A valid driver’s license.

**Preferred**

* Master’s degree in business or a related discipline.
* Lean Six Sigma Master Black Belt or equivalent depth of experience designing and delivering CI training.
* Experience at a Caterpillar dealership or in the equipment sales, service, or rental industry.
* Demonstrated curiosity and willingness to learn and apply emerging technologies, including AI, to strengthen problem solving, process improvement, decision support, and organizational productivity. Experience applying AI in these areas is preferred but not required.
* Experience building on an existing CI function and growing its influence across a multi-location organization.

****Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities****

* Strong coaching and leadership development skills; leads through influence rather than authority.
* Ability to connect improvement work to business priorities and help leaders choose where to focus.
* Curiosity about and practical comfort with AI as a business tool.
* Exceptional communication and facilitation skills with all levels, from the front line to executives.
* Ability to build and maintain trusted relationships with executives, senior managers, and teams.
* Respect for existing culture and relationships, with the judgment to improve without unnecessary disruption.
* Strong organizational, prioritization, and project management skills.
* Effective computer skills with Microsoft Office and the ability to learn proprietary systems.

****Other Requirements of Position****

* Works under broad supervision. Designs and carries out programs and far-reaching objectives independently, informing management as appropriate.
* Major responsibilities require a wide degree of creativity and latitude.
* If an error is made while in this position, it will require some effort to identify and can significantly impact the company financially.
* Frequently communicates with coworkers, customers, company executives, and management.
* Maintain equipment and supplies to avoid waste, damage to areas and equipment, and to prevent accidents.

The duties and responsibilities outlined in this posting are not exhaustive and may evolve based on business needs.
 
 
All MacAllister Machinery companies are an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer, including Disabled and Veteran applicants.
